title: Family 4: Relationships and family life
invitation: Families change over time, and relationship words carry a lot of social information. Learn the everyday vocabulary for dating, partners, engagement, marriage, separation, divorce, former partners, widowhood, and being single.
summary: Core mode teaches what the relationship words point to. Cultural mode adds how the two active languages signal gender, marriage, formality, legal status, affection, and community preferences without treating one relationship model as universal.

blocks.title: Relationship words are not one ladder
blocks.text: Dating, engaged, married, separated, divorced, widowed, and single are different kinds of relationship or life-state information. Boyfriend, girlfriend, partner, spouse, husband, and wife also signal different things about gender and marriage.

blocks.title: Let the person choose the label
blocks.text: Partner and significant other are useful gender-neutral labels; spouse is specifically marital in common English. Communities and individuals differ in which labels feel natural, formal, dated, inclusive, or legally meaningful.

blocks.title: English examples
blocks.text: They are dating. She is my girlfriend. He is my partner. They are engaged. My parents are divorced. She is his ex-wife. He is widowed. They co-parent their daughter.

blocks.title: Match the relationship or life state
Relationships in a story
blocks.text: Current Gef candidate: The Fisherman and His Wife, for husband/wife language. Preferred future Family 4 reading: The Courtship of Susan Bell, for courtship, engagement, family reaction, and marriage vocabulary.

blocks.title: Family language can change with the story
blocks.description: You can recognize the basic relationship words and ask what extra social or grammatical information the language attaches to them.
